signature.instructions:
Extract congressional job or internship listings from one bulletin chunk.

The chunk begins with the source filename on its own line, followed by
text starting at a MEM-XXX-YY job ID; treat that ID as this chunk's job id
and never carry an ID over from another chunk. Derive posting_date from
the filename and format it strictly as YYYY-MM-DD (ISO 8601). Repair OCR/ligature
damage before populating any field (e.g. "o2ice"/"O&ice" -> "office",
"sta2"/"sta5"/"sta&" -> "staff", "eEorts"/"e&orts" -> "efforts",
"enicient"/"e&icient" -> "efficient").

Format office as "Congressman/Congresswoman Name (ST-NN)" only when the
specific member and state-district are identifiable. If only a general
description (e.g., "House Democrat") or a committee name is given, leave
office as None. Format salary_info strictly as "$XX,000 per year" or
"$XX,000-$YY,000 per year". If no specific salary figure is given (even
if the position is stated as "unpaid" or "paid"), set salary_info to None.
For contact, extract only the email address or phone number if provided;
do not include titles or names (e.g., use "ny13intern@gmail.com" not
"Comm. Director at ny13intern@gmail.com").

Never leave responsibilities or qualifications empty. If no explicit
qualifications are stated in the text, infer reasonable qualifications
from the context and responsibilities, or use the fallback string
"None specified" to ensure the list is not empty. Only populate the
equal_opportunity field if a formal Equal Employment Opportunity (EEO)
statement is present (e.g., "The office is an equal opportunity employer
and does not discriminate..."); do not include general encouragement
statements (e.g., "Women and minorities are highly encouraged to apply").

Do not invent fields beyond the schema, and do not treat boilerplate or
subscribe/unsubscribe text as a listing.

fields.description: Bulletin filename on the first line, then the chunk text starting at a MEM- id
One or more job listings extracted from this chunk
